text:
ashley: quick helm question — in our umbrella chart a child values file has:
```
myservice:
  env:
    FOO: ""
```
In the template we do `{{ default "bar" .Values.myservice.env.FOO }}` but it renders an empty string instead of 'bar'. Is that expected? I want fallback to 'bar' when value is empty, and ideally prefer a runtime env var if present. any clean patterns?

matt: this is a common gotcha. Two things to watch: (1) empty string vs null in values, and (2) helm template rendering happens at client time, so you can't read the pod runtime env.

sam: fwiw, use `null` to mean unset, and `""` to mean intentionally blank. If you set `FOO: null` you can then use `coalesce` or `default` to pick a fallback.

lee: recommended pattern i use: set values to either a string or null, and in the template use `coalesce` so you can chain fallbacks. eg:
```
{{- $v := coalesce .Values.myservice.env.FOO (env "FOO") "bar" -}}
FOO: {{ $v }}
```
Note: `(env "FOO")` reads the helm client's env when rendering the chart (useful for local overrides), NOT the container runtime.

ashley: ah ok that helps. so best practice = document `null` for unset in values.yaml + use coalesce in templates.

matt: also consider doing the final fallback in the k8s manifest using `valueFrom` (secret/configMap) so cluster-level config wins at runtime. avoids trying to pull runtime values into helm templates.

sam: small nit — update values.schema.json (or values.yml comment) to allow `string|null` so maintainers know to use null when they want fallback.

lee: i'll open a tiny PR to the chart README & schema after standup :thumbsup:

ashley: cool thanks — i'll update the child values and send the chart PR, pinging for review.
